title: Copyright suits: Chuck Berry, the Beatles and the Beach Boys
summary: Gil tells of a lawyer winning money for Chuck Berry from the Beatles' publisher and suggests suing the Beach Boys.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I went to a lawyer recently about something. Krasikovsky the copyright expert and he had just gotten three hundred thousand for Chuck Berry?

Oh, they got more than that, but it took three years to get it. And also it was from the Beatles. Because you know the Beatles had been ripping him off a lot. But they like him so much and everything so they came to the hearing to court, /and said yes, they, they wanted him to win. In other words, /But they couldn't give it out of their pocket because it was the publisher. They wanted him to pay, right? He was collecting all of the money, from some of it. So the publisher had to pay for it as well as them. So they came and said, yes we cannot tell a lie, we
They have admitted that he was their greatest influence.

So ( ?) got him some money finally. So I said, go ahead, keep on going and go to the, what's the guy's name, go to the Beach Boys and make them give Chuck Berry their, half, at least half their royalties on 'Surfing USA' which was a direct copy from 'Sweet Little Sixteen'. Identical, except for the words. Even the, the whole thing.
